html:
SMTO-CTX-0038 — A task note or saved item is no longer available

GUID: d25df8e4-30f2-5b84-8a82-8e71ebaffe58
Slug: task-context-source-unavailable
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: task-context

What happened

  • The task, or a save you made, pointed to a note, message or source that is missing or can't be used here. It may have been removed or may belong to something else. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you were using Save to task context, wait until the reply has fully finished, refresh the page, then try saving it again. Only complete replies that are still part of the task can be saved as task context.
  2. Open Saved task context on the task. If an item says Remove unavailable selection to continue, select Remove next to it. A saved message that is no longer available holds the task back until it is removed.
  3. If the task hit this while reading its notes, let it continue; it is told to list what is available and pick again. The list shows only items the task can still open.
  4. If something the task needs is truly gone, select Steer and give it that information again in your own words. A missing note doesn't mean the information never existed; you can supply it directly.

What success looks like

  • The save shows as Saved · Remove, or the task reads an available note and continues.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't change access or security settings to make the item appear.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Task Context could not resolve the requested source because it is absent, no longer retained, or not accessible in the current scope (for example source_unavailable, note_not_found or saved_message_source_unavailable).

What this means

  • The requested source is absent, no longer retained, or unavailable within the current access scope. The recorded reason and operation message identify the specific condition.

Why this can happen

  • The notebook cannot resolve an authorized retained source.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the operation, reason, revision and source reference recorded by the producer.

How to fix it

  • List the parent section in Task Context to rediscover accessible sources and use a reference returned by that listing; for saved messages, the source must be a complete, context-eligible assistant message in this run. Report any remaining gap, and do not treat an unavailable source as proof that no relevant information exists or bypass access checks.
  • List the observed parent section to rediscover accessible sources. Report a remaining gap; do not treat it as proof that no relevant information exists.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the indicated argument or refresh the source first; retain existing access checks and revision checks.

How to verify the fix

  • The corrected notebook operation succeeds.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass source access checks or overwrite a revision conflict.

Technical notes

  • An unavailable source does not prove that no relevant information exists.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-CTX-0028 — SMTO couldn't find an item in this Task's saved notes
